formalin-induced neuronal activities in forebrain are more complex than those in spinal cord and dorsal root ganglion.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, in the formalin model, the forebrain networks are activated in a time-dependent manner, and their activity pattern is closely related to the pain behaviors.

, the formalin-induced neuronal activities in the forebrain are not simply a mirror of the activities in spinal dorsal horn, but are the result of the interaction among cortical and thalalamic areas, and the direction of the flow of information in these networks may change during the formalin test.

, (i), in the first hour of the formalin test, the cortical and thalamus neurons are activated by noxious stimuli and the information is conveyed from cortex to thalamic areas, and from the medial thalamus to lateral areas.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cortical and thalamocortical neuronal activity patterns are different during the first and second phase of formal test, which may underlie the different pain behavior during these phases.

the forebrain networks may serve to integrate and regulate the activity of the primary afferent and spinal cord circuits, and that the direction of information transfer may also change with the development and disappearance of central sensitization in the formalin test.
